message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_289187f12d1e", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 160, "mechanism": "The output-side synchronizer block (line 160) gates its reset on output_rst_sync3. The replacement adds `&& (read)` so the synchronizer clears wr_ptr_gray_sync only when a read actually occurs. This prevents spurious clearing of the synchronized write pointer during early cycles (cycles 0-3) where output_rst_sync3 is still asserted but no read has happened, preserving correct empty/full computation and fixing the cycle-4 input_axis_tready mismatch and the cycle-8/9 output_axis_tdata mismatches."}, {"id": "patch_8b896b0b2e36", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 163, "mechanism": "Resets the output data register (data_out_reg) in the same synchronous block that already clears rd_ptr and rd_ptr_gray on output_rst_sync3 (line 163). The observed failure shows output_axis_tdata=2 at cycle 8 (expected 1) and 3 at cycle 9 (expected 2), indicating stale data from reset was presented. Adding `data_out_reg <= 0;` clears that stale word so the first post-reset read yields clean data."}, {"id": "patch_6e2e33580da6", "failure_port": "input_axis_tready", "source_line": 122, "mechanism": "The input_rst_sync3 generation (line 122) currently clears on async_rst alone. The replacement ` (async_rst) && (!write) ` prevents the synchronizer from releasing while a write is in flight during early cycles, avoiding a one-cycle early de-assertion of input_axis_tready (cycle 4 expected 0, actual 1) and downstream pointer desynchronization that later corrupts output_axis_tdata."}, {"id": "patch_369cf8cc07c8", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 163, "mechanism": "The read enable logic (line 163) currently uses `read` directly. The replacement `(read) && (output_rst_sync3)` makes the read conditional on the output reset having fully completed, preventing a premature read during cycles 0-3 when output_rst_sync3=1 but pointers are not yet aligned. This stops the early data corruption seen at cycles 8 and 9."}, {"id": "patch_ef9da370f3e6", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 148, "mechanism": "The input-side synchronizer block (line 148) clears rd_ptr_gray_sync on input_rst_sync3. The replacement `(input_rst_sync3) && (read)` ties the clear to an actual read event, preventing the synchronizer from discarding valid write-pointer state before the output domain has consumed it. This keeps full/empty calculation correct and eliminates the output_axis_tdata drift at cycles 8/9."}, {"id": "patch_f09094005ed7", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 139, "mechanism": "The write enable (line 139) currently gates on `write` alone. The replacement `(write) && (!output_rst_sync3)` suppresses writes until the output reset has fully completed (output_rst_sync3=0). This prevents data from being written into the FIFO while the output pointers are still resetting, which otherwise causes the output_axis_tdata mismatches at cycles 8 and 9."}, {"id": "patch_c4126d267998", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 148, "mechanism": "The input-side synchronizer (line 148) qualifies its reset with `output_rst_sync3` via `(input_rst_sync3) && (output_rst_sync3)`. This ensures the input domain does not clear its synchronized read pointer until the output domain has also finished reset, maintaining pointer coherence across clock domains and fixing the output_axis_tdata sequence."}, {"id": "patch_74d6b0b1b314", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 160, "mechanism": "The output-side synchronizer (line 160) changes its reset gate from `output_rst_sync3` to `(output_rst_sync3) && (!write)`. This prevents the synchronizer from clearing the write-pointer gray code while a write is occurring, avoiding a race that corrupts the full/empty calculation and subsequently the output_axis_tdata stream at cycles 8/9."}], "explanation": "The three observed mismatches (cycle-4 input_axis_tready early assertion; cycle-8 output_axis_tdata=2 vs 1; cycle-9 output_axis_tdata=3 vs 2) point to two root causes: (1) input-side reset releasing one cycle too early, and (2) output-side data register and pointer synchronizers not being cleared or gated tightly enough during the multi-cycle reset sequence. The top candidate (patch_289187f12d1e) directly addresses the output synchronizer by requiring a real read before clearing wr_ptr_gray_sync, which aligns the empty/full calculation with actual data movement. The second candidate (patch_8b896b0b2e36) adds the missing data_out_reg reset in the same block, eliminating the stale first word. The third candidate (patch_6e2e33580da6) fixes the input_rst_sync3 gate to wait for write quiescence, correcting the early tready. The remaining candidates each tighten a different cross-domain gate (write, read, or pointer sync) so that reset completion in one domain is acknowledged before the other domain advances its pointers. Only one of these gates needs to be corrected in silicon; they are ranked by how directly their line appears in the failing simulation trace."}
